$comment: The knowledge base's identity as every reader must compute it from <dir>/.semiont/config. Go (apps/launcher/internal/launcher: effectiveKBName, committedDomain, didWeb, kbResource) and TypeScript (packages/core: SemiontProject name and siteDomain, kbDid, kbResource) each run every case and fail on any difference; Rust (packages/sdk-rust: kb_did, and kb_resource, the audience the gateway's tokens must carry) runs every case with a domain. `config` null means the file is absent; `domain`, `did` and `resource` null mean no identity is declared. Add a case here before changing either implementation.

cases.config:
[project]
name = "ArXiv Research Papers"

[git]
sync = true

[site]
domain = "the-ai-alliance.github.io:semiont-arxiv-kb"
siteName = "ArXiv Research Papers"
cases.name: ArXiv Research Papers

cases.why: no config file: the directory name, and no identity
cases.name: bare-kb

cases.why: an empty name counts as none
cases.name: empty-name-kb

cases.why: a key that merely starts with name, in a section above [project]
cases.name: The Real Name

cases.why: an inline comment is not part of the value
cases.name: Commented

cases.why: an equals sign inside the value
cases.name: a = b

cases.why: a dotted key names the same table
cases.name: Dotted

cases.why: the domain is the top-level [site] only, never an environment's
cases.name: Env Scoped

cases.why: a [site] without a domain declares no identity
cases.name: No Domain

cases.why: a multi-segment domain becomes a multi-segment path
cases.name: Deep

cases.why: malformed TOML counts as no file
cases.name: broken-kb
